Bone marrow aspirate smears (Wright–Giemsa). The blasts are variably larger than red blood cells. The nuclei show irregular nuclear contours and finely dispersed chromatin. Nucleoli are typically indistinct. Pale vacuoles (<<36871>>) and fine granules (<<36868>>) are noted.
